key_insight: Wind shear and veer can cut actuator-disk power efficiency by more than 20% because they change both the effective inflow speed and the rotor’s induction physics.
engineering_relevance: Accurate wind-turbine power prediction in the atmospheric boundary layer must account for shear- and veer-induced aerodynamic losses, not just rotor-equivalent wind speed.
method: Concurrent-precursor LES of an actuator disk turbine in stratified ABL conditions
Controlled simplified inflow LES with shear and veer varied independently
Decomposition of performance changes into geometric vs. inductive effects
evidence_signal: The study uses large-eddy simulations and reports that shear and veer effects can reduce the power coefficient by more than 20%, with controlled cases used to isolate the mechanisms.
watch_item: The findings are from actuator-disk LES, so translating the mechanisms directly to real rotors and engineering models may require further validation.
paper_title: Influence of wind shear and veer on power, thrust, and induction of an actuator disk
